desc:
An independent set of a tree is a set of nodes in which no two nodes are directly connected by an edge (no node is chosen together with its parent). The empty set counts as an independent set.

Return the number of independent sets of the tree, modulo 1,000,000,007.

Only the shape of the tree matters, so every node in the input has value 0.

How trees are given. A binary tree is passed as an integer array in level order (top to bottom, left to right). The first entry is the root. After that, the left and right child of every existing node are written in turn; a missing child is written as -1 (real node values are never negative). Missing nodes have no children listed, and trailing -1 entries are dropped.

For example, [1,2,3,-1,4] is the tree whose root 1 has children 2 and 3; node 2 has no left child and has 4 as its right child; node 3 is a leaf.

Example 1

tree = [0,0,0]
Output: 5
The sets are {}, {root}, {left}, {right} and {left, right}.

Example 2

tree = [0,0,-1,0,-1,0]
Output: 8
A path of 4 nodes has 8 independent sets.
constraints: The array follows the encoding above exactly
hints: Brute force over subsets is exponential. Think about one node and decide whether it is in the set or not.
Per node keep two counts for its subtree: inc[u] (sets that contain u) and exc[u] (sets that do not). The subtrees of the two children are independent, so counts multiply.

If u is chosen, each child must be left out: inc[u] = product of exc[c]. If not, each child is free: exc[u] = product of (inc[c] + exc[c]). A missing child contributes a factor of 1. Reduce modulo 109+7.
editorial: Count by cases on the node. Sets containing u may not contain any child of u, but may do anything below the children's children, which is exactly what exc[c] counts for each child. Sets not containing u combine any independent set of the left subtree with any independent set of the right subtree, giving the product of inc[c] + exc[c].

For a leaf inc = exc = 1. The answer is inc[root] + exc[root] modulo 109+7. One bottom-up pass gives O(n) time and O(n) memory. For a path of n nodes this reproduces the Fibonacci numbers, a good sanity check.
